messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Physical Distances and QTL Mapping
parts:
We really need genetic distances. You can approximate genetic distances using physical distances, but you may get better results if you re-estimate the inter-marker distances using est.map().

karl

> Can I use physical distances for QTL mapping in R/qtl?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Physical Distances and QTL Mapping
parts:
Yes, but it's best to convert to genetic distances after merging the two sets of markers. 

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Physical Distances and QTL Mapping
parts:
Look at the tutorials, such as the genetic map tutorial: http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/geneticmaps.pdf

If you have dense markers, you might try just converting Mbp -> cM assuming a constant recombination rate. est.map() can be quite slow with dense markers.

karl
